column3: Close to the Greek; “lepta” is rendered “mites.”
NKJV includes “for God,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “put in gifts.”
Close to the Greek; “led astray” is rendered “deceived.”
Close to the Greek; “governors” is rendered “rulers.”
NKJV has “settle it in your hearts,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “settle it therefore.”
NKJV has “contradict or resist,” the reverse of the Greek order “resist nor contradict.”
NKJV has the imperative “possess,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the future “you will gain.”
NKJV has “the sea and the waves roaring,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “at the roar of the sea and the waves.”
Close to the Greek; “fainting” is rendered “hearts failing them.”
